title: A Bridge Without a River

plate.narration: Stone arches rise from the silt beside a dry channel. No river passes under them now. From the firm bank, the old bridge stretches away into a haze of salt and pale mud.

goal.text: Solve the missing-river mystery from the bank.

steps.label: Find firm ground to work from
Get a look under the arches
Show the guide what you found

bank.narration: A Skupper guide stops above a dry riverbed. "Buried bridge," says the guide. "No river. Still not walking on it." Master Orin Vale, the griffin Riftseeker you met on the glacier, brushes grit from an arch. His next brushful lands on his own foot. "A very dusty discovery."

choices.label: Ask Orin what he has found

orin.narration: "This grit matches the glacier," says Orin. "Perhaps water came through a rift." Across the bridge stands a sealed door. "That stays shut. Today we have one question: where did the river go?" He opens his notebook. Will you share your listening chime readings, or keep them private?

choices.label: Share the listening chime's readings with Orin
Keep your readings and compare the stonework

share.narration: You sound the listening chime. Orin copies its rhythm beside his glacier notes. "Thank you. A sound we can compare." He draws an ear. It looks rather like a cabbage.

choices.label: Inspect the bridge from the bank

keep.narration: You keep your chime readings private. Orin puts his pencil away. "Fair enough. The stones have plenty to tell us." A sprinkle of grit lands on his foot again. "Rather persistently."

choices.label: Inspect the bridge from the bank

guide_limits.narration: Your guide plants both front fins in the wet mud at the edge of the bank. "This far. No farther." You mark a stopping line on dry ground. Orin sets his tools behind it. "Even my brush stays on this side." A trickle runs through a little groove below the shelf. "The tide reaches this pocket later," the guide says. "We have time to look, then we pack up. No crossing." Orin turns to you. "Then let us make a proper little expedition."

choices.label: Find our work spot

ground_test.narration: Orin has a short measuring stick and a coil of plain cord beside his bag. From dry ground, you test three nearby patches. Shells wobble. Dark mud squelches. The rock shelf stays firm. Share your clues and mark the patches from nearest the water to farthest away.

interaction.cue: Put the patches in order, starting beside the water.
clues: The dark mud touches the water.
The shells sit between the mud and the rock shelf.
Our work spot is the rock shelf, farthest from the water.

onSuccess.narration: You mark the rock shelf. Everyone and every tool fit behind the stopping line.

onFailure.narration: The guide points from water to mud, shells, then rock. You correct the marks and gather on the firm shelf.

onAssisted.narration: Together you follow the guide: mud, shells, rock. The firm shelf is your work spot.

work.narration: Loose silt covers the nearest arch. You can brush it away from the bank, or hold a viewing plank steady while a friend looks down. Both keep you behind the stopping line. Which job sounds better?

choices.label: Brush out a buried clue
Hold a viewing plank together
Let our thornguard brace the plank

variants.text: Your fixed rail gives you a ready viewing support. The kit still has to be carried by hand.
Your sled keeps the kit together. For a mirror view, you will need to hold a temporary plank support.

clear.narration: Under the dust: a waterline carved into the arch, and smooth river pebbles below it. But the riverbed is dry. Orin draws all three. "A bridge. A riverbed. A missing river." The guide leans closer from the bank.

choices.label: Draw the waterline and dry channel

brace.narration: In the mirror you spot smooth river pebbles beneath the arches. A waterline marks the stone above them. Today the riverbed is dry. Orin sketches the view. "A bridge. A riverbed. A missing river."

choices.label: Draw the waterline and dry channel

river_explain.narration: The waterline and smooth river pebbles appear in your notes beside the dry channel. "What do they tell us?" asks Orin. Fit the clues into a little story. The shut door offers no answers today.

interaction.cue: Order the clues: what the water left, what it wore smooth, what we see today.
clues: Start with the mark high on the stone.
The smooth pebbles come between the waterline and the dry bed.
Finish with what the riverbed looks like now.

onSuccess.narration: Water once flowed beneath these arches. Now it is gone from here. Where it went is still a mystery.

onFailure.narration: Orin lays the drawing beside the stones: waterline, worn pebbles, dry bed. You fix the order together. An old river flowed here. Where it went is still a mystery.

restore_bank.narration: Time to pack up. Bring the board and cord back from whichever job they did. Loose silt stays on the dry side. Everyone choose a last job. The guide checks the upper return path while Orin counts his kit aloud. "One notebook. One brush. Two sandwiches. A remarkable improvement on last Tuesday."

interaction.cue: Everyone choose a job before we leave.

options.label: Pack the brush
options.reaction: Orin checks his bag. "Brush: one. Dust: several million."

options.label: Roll up the cord
options.reaction: You coil the cord. It finally stops trying to tie itself to Orin.

options.label: Mark the stopping line
options.reaction: The guide checks your stones. "Good. A warning I can use."

guide_handover.narration: You show the guide the waterline, the river pebbles, and your stopping line. "An old river," the guide repeats. "Still no bridge tours." Orin hands over a copy of the sketch. Nobody has to cross to see what you found.

choices.label: Take our missing-river clue onward

variants.text: Your tested signs leave a public viewing point on the high bank. The guide has the useful copy; Orin has his own field notes.
Orin carries the careful copy to the Riftseekers. Your closed-work-area sign asks visitors to wait for a later visit.
You label the drawing as rebuilt after the tide and leave out the lost fine measurements.

rest.narration: You draw the arches, the waterline, and the dry riverbed on one page. The river this bridge served is gone from here. Orin copies only what the stones show. The sealed door remains shut. Your guide leads you back along the firm bank.

variants.text: Behind you, the guide lays your local sketch beside the stopping sign. People can learn from the high bank without setting foot on the bridge.
The work area is closed behind you. Orin tucks the research copy inside his cloak, ready to compare this missing river with other finds.
You saved the original measurements and rebuilt the washed-out markers before leaving.
You kept the return route clear and rebuilt a simpler drawing after the tide soaked the original.

brush_clue.narration: You reach with a long brush from the rock shelf. A pale mark peeks through the dust. Orin holds a cloth under it. "Brush the stone, please. My feet are quite clean enough."

interaction.cue: Tap when the marker reaches the gold.

onFailure.narration: Pffft! Your brush catches a dust pocket. Orin sneezes, then helps clear the last handful. The mark is visible.

hold_plank.narration: The viewing plank rests between two firm rocks behind the stopping line. Hold it steady while a friend uses a little mirror to look beneath the arch. "My tail is not a spare support," Orin says, moving it.

interaction.cue: Hold the plank while your friend lifts the mirror.

braced_plank.narration: Your thornguard braces the plank against the firm rocks. The mirror gives everyone a clear view beneath the arch. Orin folds his tail safely away. "Excellent. All supports accounted for."

choices.label: Look under the arch

equipment.narration: Orin has one broad board and enough cord for one job. Fix the board as a viewing rail, and everyone can study the arch together. Make it a carrying sled, and you can move the drawings and tools quickly if the tide creeps up. You cannot build both. "I packed two sandwiches," says Orin. "Apparently that is not the same thing as two boards." Which will you prepare?

choices.label: Build a fixed viewing rail
Build a portable kit sled

build_rail.narration: The guide points out three sound posts on the dry shelf. Pass the cord along them, one hero at a time, while Orin sets the board on the supports. The rail will stay here until you leave. You give it a gentle test from the dry side. Orin leans on it, nods, and carefully retrieves the sandwich he left underneath.

interaction.cue: Catch and pass the cord along the dry-side posts.

onSuccess.narration: The rail stays solid. Your viewing spot will be ready when the tide reaches the lower groove.

onFailure.narration: The rail stays solid. Your viewing spot will be ready when the tide reaches the lower groove.

onAssisted.narration: The rail stays solid. Your viewing spot will be ready when the tide reaches the lower groove.

build_sled.narration: The board rests on two short runners from Orin's kit. Put the bag in the middle and level your sides before sliding it. The guide shows a dry parking place behind a rock. Orin adds his notebook, then removes his sandwich. "Important equipment. Separate pocket." The sled can move, but it cannot serve as a fixed rail.

interaction.cue: Raise or lower your side until the kit sled is level.

onSuccess.narration: The loaded sled slides neatly into its dry parking place. It will be useful if you must move things in a hurry.

onFailure.narration: The loaded sled slides neatly into its dry parking place. It will be useful if you must move things in a hurry.

onAssisted.narration: The loaded sled slides neatly into its dry parking place. It will be useful if you must move things in a hurry.

water_question.narration: Orin turns the drawing so everyone can see. "The waterline is up here. The round pebbles are down there. But that new trickle smells salty." The guide dips a fin into the low groove. "Tide water. This old riverbed is much bigger." You have two different stories in one place: an old river, and a little tide arriving today. Test the little groove before mixing them up.

choices.label: Watch the groove through a whole pulse

watch_pulse.narration: A scrap of reed turns in the groove. Water pushes it forward, pauses, then pulls it back. The guide marks one edge with a shell. Wait for the reed to return to that mark, then call it. Orin watches a different reed. It remains perfectly still. "That one is my pencil," he admits.

interaction.cue: Tap in the gold when the reed returns to the shell mark.

onSuccess.narration: The reed comes back to the same shell. The guide watches a second pulse and confirms it: today's little tide moves both ways.

onFailure.narration: You call a little early. The guide keeps the shell in place and helps you watch the next complete pulse. The reed comes back; this tide moves both ways.

onAssisted.narration: The reed comes back to the same shell. The guide watches a second pulse and confirms it: today's little tide moves both ways.

compare_pulse.narration: Orin puts three covered sample pots on dry stone: glacier grit, fresh tide mud, and dust from the arch. He shows you the glacier pot first. A gust blows his labels loose. While he catches them, he moves the pots out of the wind. Keep track of the glacier sample so you can compare it with the arch dust. "The lids are excellent," he says. "The handwriting is airborne."

interaction.cue: Watch the glacier sample as Orin moves the covered pots.

onSuccess.narration: You find the glacier pot. Side by side, its pale grit looks like the dust from the arch. The tide mud is darker. Today's little salty tide moves both ways; it does not explain the high old waterline or the river-worn pebbles.

onFailure.narration: Orin lifts the lids and helps you find the glacier sample. Its pale grit looks like the arch dust; the tide mud is darker. Today's little tide does not explain the old waterline and river-worn pebbles.

onAssisted.narration: You label each pot together before comparing the pale glacier grit with the arch dust. The darker tide mud is different. Today's little tide does not explain the old riverbed.

tide_turn.narration: Plip. Water reaches the lower tool shelf sooner than expected. Everyone is already on the high rock shelf, but a tray of drawings sits low beside the return path. There is time to do one job first. Save the drawings, and the path markers will need rebuilding. Secure the return path, and the drawings will get wet; you will have to piece their marks together. Orin holds both sandwiches above his head. "I have secured lunch. What first?"

choices.label: Save the drawings; rebuild the path afterward
Secure the path; reconstruct the wet drawings

save_records.narration: You choose the drawings. The little tide runs under the low tray while you stay on the high shelf. Use the equipment you prepared. The guide watches the water and calls a stop if it reaches the next shell. The far bank and the sealed door stay well beyond your work.

choices.label: Use our fixed rail to lift the tray
Bring the tray back on a carrying board

rail_lift.narration: Your fixed rail holds firm. One friend supports the long lifting cord while another tips the tray toward the high shelf. Orin is ready with a dry cloth. A page starts to curl. "No flying lessons today," he tells it. Keep the cord steady until the whole tray reaches the cloth.

interaction.cue: Hold the lifting cord while your friend brings the tray in.

onSuccess.narration: The drawings arrive dry. The low path markers have washed loose, so you must rebuild the return route.

onFailure.narration: The drawings arrive dry. The low path markers have washed loose, so you must rebuild the return route.

onAssisted.narration: The drawings arrive dry. The low path markers have washed loose, so you must rebuild the return route.

sled_lift.narration: Your carrying board slides beneath the tray from the high side. Level the board so the drawings do not slip as you bring them back. Orin reaches for the notebook, then checks with you before lifting it. The guide stays at the marked shell, watching the water rather than asking anyone to hurry.

interaction.cue: Level the drawing sled before bringing it back.

onSuccess.narration: The drawings arrive dry. Your sled helped save them, but the low path markers have washed loose.

onFailure.narration: The drawings arrive dry. Your sled helped save them, but the low path markers have washed loose.

onAssisted.narration: The drawings arrive dry. Your sled helped save them, but the low path markers have washed loose.

variants.text: You choose to change your plan: take the board off its fixed posts and lash it to the spare runners. The viewing rail is gone; you now have a carrying sled.

path_repair.narration: The old markers have rolled into the wet groove. The guide calls a different route along the high shelf: start behind the tall rock, pass the split post, then reach the dry steps. Each hero can see a different landmark. Tell one another what you see and lay out the return route before moving the kit.

interaction.cue: Plan the dry route from the work shelf to the steps.
clues: The split post comes after the rock and before the steps.

onSuccess.narration: You mark the upper route. The return path is ready again, and the drawings are dry.

onFailure.narration: The guide points out the upper route one landmark at a time. You correct the order and mark it together.

onAssisted.narration: You mark the upper route. The return path is ready again, and the drawings are dry.

save_path.narration: You choose the return path. The lowest marker wobbles in the water. Keep everyone on the high shelf and move the warning back before it falls. Your drawings will get wet while you do this. Orin looks at the tray, then at the path. "People first. We can draw again." How will your prepared equipment help?

choices.label: Secure the upper warning to our fixed rail
Move the warning on a carrying board

rail_warning.narration: The rail makes a sturdy anchor for the new warning. Hold the cord while a friend secures the marker on the high side. The guide checks that it points toward the dry steps. Below you, the tray gives a soft splash. Orin winces. "That was the notebook. I do hope the cabbage ear can swim."

interaction.cue: Hold the warning cord while your friend ties the marker.

onSuccess.narration: The upper return path stays clearly marked. The drawings are wet, and you will need to reconstruct their details.

onFailure.narration: The upper return path stays clearly marked. The drawings are wet, and you will need to reconstruct their details.

onAssisted.narration: The upper return path stays clearly marked. The drawings are wet, and you will need to reconstruct their details.

sled_warning.narration: Load the warning board onto your sled. Pass its guide cord from friend to friend along the upper shelf so it never swings into the wet groove. At the dry steps, Orin wedges the marker between two sound rocks. Down below, the notebook takes a small, undignified bath.

interaction.cue: Catch and pass the guide cord along the high shelf.

onSuccess.narration: The upper return path stays clearly marked. The wet drawings will need to be pieced together.

onFailure.narration: The upper return path stays clearly marked. The wet drawings will need to be pieced together.

onAssisted.narration: The upper return path stays clearly marked. The wet drawings will need to be pieced together.

variants.text: You choose to change your plan: take the board off the rail posts and lash it to the spare runners. The fixed rail becomes a carrying sled.

wet_notes.narration: You lift the wet sheets onto the high shelf. Before Orin separates them, look at the marks you copied: an arch, a high waterline, rounded pebbles, and an empty channel. Remember the pattern, then rebuild the sketch together. The guide keeps the original stonework in view, so a forgotten mark can always be checked.

interaction.cue: Watch the four marks, then rebuild the sketch.

onSuccess.narration: You rebuild the sketch and check it against the arch. The fine measurements are washed away; label this copy as a reconstruction.

onFailure.narration: One mark is out of place. The guide points to the arch, waterline, pebbles and dry channel. You check and redraw them. The fine measurements are gone, so this is a reconstruction.

onAssisted.narration: You rebuild the sketch and check it against the arch. The fine measurements are washed away; label this copy as a reconstruction.

records_review.narration: You spread the pages on dry stone and check every hero, every tool, and the return markers. The guide shakes water off one fin. Orin shakes water off his brush. Only one of them splashes the notebook. "Sorry," says Orin. The guide says nothing at all, which is somehow worse. You have enough evidence to explain the old river, even if today changed your plans.

choices.label: Make our river explanation

variants.text: Your original drawings and measurements are dry. You can give Orin a precise copy, but had to spend time rebuilding the return path.
The return path stayed marked throughout. Your rebuilt sketch shows the main clues, but the fine measurements must wait for a later visit.

record_decision.narration: Orin can make one careful extra copy before you leave. Give it to the guide, and your group can help mark a public viewing point on the high bank. Send it with Orin, and other Riftseekers can compare the missing river with their own finds; the work area here will stay closed until someone returns. Your private chime readings stay private either way. Who needs this copy first?

choices.label: Open a marked bank viewpoint for local visitors
Send the careful copy with Orin; close this work area

visitor_plan.narration: Make the viewpoint useful without turning it into a bridge crossing. The guide has a waiting-place sign, a sketch of the waterline, and a return arrow. Put them where a visitor needs them: stop first, look from the high bank, then return by the dry steps. "Could add a tea stall," Orin suggests. The guide looks at the mud. "No."

interaction.cue: Arrange the visitor signs in the order people need them.

options.label: Look at the waterline from the high bank

clues: People must see the stopping line before looking at the bridge.
The view comes between waiting and returning.
The dry steps are the way out, not a way onto the bridge.

onSuccess.narration: The signs make a complete bank visit. Try them with Orin before leaving.

onFailure.narration: The guide moves the stopping sign to the start. You correct the rest together, then test the visit.

onAssisted.narration: The signs make a complete bank visit. Try them with Orin before leaving.

visitor_trial.narration: Orin pretends he has never been here. He walks to the stopping sign and peers at your sketch. "Where do I put my feet?" Everyone chooses a useful part of the welcome. The guide listens. If your words offer a bridge crossing, she stops the pretend tour and helps you correct it.

interaction.cue: Everyone help Orin try the marked viewpoint.

options.label: Show him the waiting line
options.reaction: Orin plants both feet behind it. "Even the dusty foot?" Yes, that one too.

options.label: Point out the waterline and pebbles
options.reaction: Orin follows your pointing hand from the arch to the old riverbed. "I can see it from here."

options.label: Show him the dry return steps
options.reaction: Orin follows the arrow back to the steps. The guide nods: a visit with a way home.

onSuccess.narration: The viewpoint stays open on the high bank. Your guide keeps the local copy; Orin will compare his own notes later.

onFailure.narration: The viewpoint stays open on the high bank. Your guide keeps the local copy; Orin will compare his own notes later.

onAssisted.narration: The viewpoint stays open on the high bank. Your guide keeps the local copy; Orin will compare his own notes later.

research_plan.narration: Prepare a page another investigator can understand without you beside it. Put the old waterline first, the rounded riverbed pebbles next, then the dry channel you saw today. Mark the sealed door as unvisited. Orin adds a box for questions. It is much larger than the box for answers. "Room to grow," he says.

interaction.cue: Build an evidence page, ending with the limit of your visit.

options.label: An old waterline marks the arch
The far door was not visited

clues: Begin with the mark on the arch.
The pebbles go after the waterline and before today's dry channel.
The unvisited door belongs last, under things we did not test.

onSuccess.narration: The page separates what you saw from what you do not know.

onFailure.narration: You compare the page with the visible arch and fix the order. The far door stays in the unvisited box.

onAssisted.narration: The page separates what you saw from what you do not know.

copy_relay.narration: Pass the wrapped copy along the dry shelf to Orin. Each friend checks that its corner is tucked inside the cover before passing it. The guide rolls a closed-work-area sign into place. "Visitors wait for a later trip," she says. Orin accepts the packet with both hands. His sandwich has finally found its proper pocket.

interaction.cue: Catch the wrapped page and pass it toward Orin.

onSuccess.narration: Orin has the careful research copy. The local work area stays closed, with a warning at its entrance.

onFailure.narration: Orin has the careful research copy. The local work area stays closed, with a warning at its entrance.

onAssisted.narration: Orin has the careful research copy. The local work area stays closed, with a warning at its entrance.

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny, curious, with real consequences. Describe actions and sensory details directly. Short dialogue. Never use "the kind of thing that", "the sort of thing that", or "it was X, the type of thing that makes you Y" comparisons. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.
